title: Converting rates and squared/cubed units
subtitle: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units · 15 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **15 of the official questions in Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units are this one** — 4 Easy, 5 Medium, 6 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Hard tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The unit has 'per' in it (feet per second, yards per hour, miles per hour) and only one part changes.
- Or the unit is 'square ___' or 'cubic ___' and the question gives a linear conversion factor.
- The answer is often a decimal or a grid-in to the nearest tenth.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Convert only the part of the unit that changes, and leave the other part (for example 'per hour') alone.
- 2) For area, apply the linear factor twice (square it).
- For volume, apply it three times (cube it).
- 3) Round only at the very end, to the precision the question asks for.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the full expression, such as value*(factor)^2, so you don't round midway.
It won't catch a missing square.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: For area or volume, you apply the linear factor once instead of squaring or cubing it.
For rates, you convert both parts, or you flip the factor and divide.
Rounding an intermediate value also pushes a nearest-tenth grid-in off by 0.1.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
For area or volume, you apply the linear factor once instead of squaring or cubing it.
For rates, you convert both parts, or you flip the factor and divide.
